text:
maya: Heads-up — intake for a new candidate model: odyssey11b (11B). Goal: quick perf + quality smoke so PMs can decide prioritization. Requesting: ctx sweeps (512/2048/8192), batching profile (1/2/4/8), and int4 quant (q4_int4) vsfp16 baseline. Can someone pick this up?

ravi: I can take perf lead. plan to run a small matrix later today. any must-have eval sets?

maya: thanks. start with convo-bench (latency), summarization-100 (ROUGE), and unit-qa (exact match). We care about tail latency >95pct and throughput at steady state.

jordyn: FYI our quant tool is the newer qtool-v2 — it has a --kv-swap flag that helps 8k ctx on A100. Will try that if OOMs.

tess: tag me for regression alerts. want to see eval diffs against our current stable (tempest11b) as baseline.

ravi: kickoff notes: running on a single node: A100-80GB, driver image: rinf-bench:2026-03-20, commit: d3fa9b. command:
```
./run_bench --model odyssey11b --mode quant --quant q4_int4 --ctx 2048 --batch 4 --warmup 100 --iters 100 --out s3://redwood-ml/bench/2101234567/
```
will post logs + perf once done.

bench-bot: build queued on gpu-pool-09, estimated start in ~3m.

ravi: quick smoke results (2048 ctx / batch4):
- fp16 baseline: p50=38ms p95=124ms throughput=98 tok/s
- q4_int4: p50=31ms p95=160ms throughput=120 tok/s
notes: int4 shows better median latency and throughput but p95 regressed (more tail jitter).

maya: interesting — tail went up. any logs?

ravi: attaching snippet of runtime log:
```
[2026-03-20 14:12:03] KV cache miss spikes during generation step 7-12, batching occasionally triggers kernel fallback to generic path.
OOMs not observed at 2048 but saw high mem fragmentation.
```

jordyn: can you try enabling --kv-swap and run ctx=8192 smoke with bs=1? curious if tail is caused by cache pressure.

ravi: started 8192/bs1 run. command: `./run_bench --model odyssey11b --quant q4_int4 --ctx 8192 --batch 1 --kv-swap true`

bench-bot: run finished. summary uploaded to s3://redwood-ml/bench/2101234567/8192_bs1_q4/summary.json

ravi: 8192 results w/kv-swap:
- q4_int4: p50=85ms p95=420ms throughput=45 tok/s
- Notes: without kv-swap we OOM'd on 8192. With kv-swap we stayed up but p95 high due to async swap stalls.

liam: can we test hybrid strategy: fp16 for early layers + int4 for later layers? that's reduced tail in past models. file: experiments/hybrid-layer-split-2101234567.yaml

maya: that's worth a quick probe. prioritize: 1) ensure non-oom 8k runs, 2) measure p95 degradation cause, 3) quality delta vs fp16.

ravi: quality smoke (summarization-100):
- fp16 baseline ROUGE-L: 41.2
- q4_int4 ROUGE-L: 38.7 (7% relative drop)
- notes: hallucination increase on long-context summarization; sample diffs in s3://redwood-ml/bench/2101234567/qual_diffs/

tess: 7% is non-trivial. add this to regression dashboard and mark as potential blocker for immediate rollout.

jordyn: small checklist for bring-up:
1) confirm kernel fallbacks in trace (ravi)
2) run hybrid-layer split (liam)
3) try alternate quant params (qtool-v2 --quantize-block 128/256) (jordyn)
4) run 512/2048/8192 sweeps with steady-state warmup (1000 tokens) (ravi)
5) run evals (conv/summ/qa) and post diffs (maya/tess)
6) open a model-gate PR with perf/quality artifacts (owner: maya)

maya: timeline: aim for initial triage by EOD tomorrow. if quality regression persists >5% on critical sets, deprioritize for hosted rollout.

ravi: I'll post incremental artifacts: s3://redwood-ml/bench/2101234567/{fp16_baseline,q4_int4,hybrid_split}/ and a short runbook: /contrib/bench/odyssey11b_README.md

ops-bot: deployment note — Dedicated pools may need kernel parameter `NV_GPU_MEMORY_MANAGEMENT=auto` for hybrid runs; check infra quotas before large sweep.

maya: thanks all — owners: ravi (perf), liam (hybrid), jordyn (quant tuning), tess/maya (quality review). I'll open the intake ticket and tag team leads.

liam: quick ask — can someone reserve an extra A100 on gpu-pool-09 for hybrid experiments tomorrow morning?

ravi: done, reserved gpu-pool-09:gpu-21 for 09:00 UTC.

maya: perfect. will sync in tomorrow standup. :thumbsup:
